title: SERA: Scale-Equalized Rollout Allocation for Maximum Likelihood Reinforcement Learning
abstract: arXiv:2609.36552v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Maximum Likelihood Reinforcement Learning (MaxRL) targets prompt-wise log-success and has shown strong performance on reasoning tasks. Under finite rollout budgets, however, the estimator used by MaxRL attenuates each prompt's likelihood gradient by a factor that depends on its success probability and rollout count. Under uniform rollout allocation, the common rollout count fails to compensate for success-dependent attenuation, leaving low-success prompts more strongly attenuated and distorting their relative contributions to the expected aggregate gradient. We introduce SERA (Scale-Equalized Rollout Allocation), which redistributes a fixed rollout budget to approximately equalize these finite-rollout scaling factors. translated_title: SERA：面向最大似然强化学习的尺度均衡化Rollout分配
translated_abstract: 最大似然强化学习（MaxRL）以逐提示（prompt-wise）的对数成功率为优化目标，并在推理任务上展现出强大的性能。然而在有限的rollout预算下，MaxRL所使用的估计器会依据每个提示的成功概率和rollout数量，以相应的因子衰减其似然梯度。在均匀rollout分配下，统一的rollout数量无法补偿这种依赖于成功率的衰减，导致低成功率提示受到更强的衰减，并扭曲了它们对期望聚合梯度的相对贡献。我们提出了SERA（尺度均衡化Rollout分配，Scale-Equalized Rollout Allocation），它在固定的rollout预算下重新分配资源，以近似均衡这些有限rollout的缩放因子。基于我们对有限rollout如何扭曲逐提示似然梯度的理论分析，我们将该分配问题表述为一个固定预算的max–min问题，并推导出其连续松弛问题的水平线解法……（原文摘要至此被截断）
tldr: 提出SERA方法，通过重新分配固定的rollout预算来近似均衡有限rollout造成的逐提示梯度衰减缩放因子，从而纠正最大似然强化学习中的梯度扭曲并提升推理任务表现。
en_tdlr: SERA redistributes a fixed rollout budget to approximately equalize the success-dependent finite-rollout attenuation scaling factors, correcting the distortion of prompt-wise likelihood gradients in Maximum Likelihood Reinforcement Learning.
